entry.title: CambridgeFlower Selected for SPRIND Composite Learning Challenge

link.title: CambridgeFlower Selected for SPRIND Composite Learning Challenge

entry.summary: The CambridgeFlower team has been selected for Stage 1 of the SPRIND Composite Learning Challenge to develop scalable, decentralized AI using the Flower framework.

entry.title: Prof. Nic Lane Awarded RAEng Chair in Emerging Technologies

link.title: Prof. Nic Lane Awarded RAEng Chair in Emerging Technologies

entry.summary: Professor Nic Lane has been awarded a £2.5M RAEng Chair in Emerging Technologies to develop decentralised, privacy-preserving AI as part of his new project, DANTE.

entry.title: Professor Nic Lane’s Team Wins UK-US Prize for Privacy Tech Against Financial Crime

link.title: Professor Nic Lane’s Team Wins UK-US Prize for Privacy Tech Against Financial Crime

entry.summary: Professor Nic Lane’s team was named joint winner of the UK-US PETs Challenge for developing a privacy-preserving AI solution to combat international money laundering.

entry.title: Launching the Flower Federated Learning Tool

link.title: Launching the Flower Federated Learning Tool

entry.summary: At this week’s google FL workshop, we are announcing our open source tool that makes it easier to devise and evaluate FL algorithms under real-world conditions: [http://flower.dev](http://flower.dev). The paper can be found [on arxiv](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2007.14390).

entry.title: Research Group is Moving to Cambridge

link.title: Research Group is Moving to Cambridge

entry.summary: Our research group is moving to the [Department of Computer Science and Technology](https://www.cst.cam.ac.uk/) at the [University of Cambridge](https://www.cam.ac.uk/) for the beginning of the 2020-2021 academic year.

entry.title: Talk by Shangzhe Wu
entry.summary: Shangzhe Wu presented their work on “Unsupervised Learning of Probably Symmetric Deformable 3D Objects from Images in the Wild” which was awarded Best Paper at CVPR 2020!

entry.title: Talk by Miltos Allamanis
entry.summary: Miltos Allamanis visited on 11 February 2020 and gave a talk on [Analyzing Source Code using Graph Neural Networks and Natural Language](http://www.cs.ox.ac.uk/seminars/2308.html).

entry.title: Talk by Andreas Soleiman
